Committee membership is consistent with the following conditions: If Guzman serves on the finance committee, then Hawking serves on the incentives committee. If Lepp serves on the finance committee, then Miyauchi and Upchurch both serve on the incentives committee. Wharton serves on a different committee from the one on which Zhu serves. Upchurch serves on a different committee from the one on which Guzman serves. If Zhu serves on the finance committee, so does Hawking.
question: If Guzman serves on the incentives committee, then which one of the following must be true?
options: A) Hawking serves on the finance committee.
B) Lepp serves on the incentives committee.
C) Miyauchi serves on the finance committee.
D) Wharton serves on the incentives committee.
E) Zhu serves on the finance committee.
raw_logic_programs:
# Declarations
people = EnumSort([Guzman, Hawking, Lepp, Miyauchi, Upchurch, Wharton, Zhu])
committees = EnumSort([finance, incentives])
serves = Function([people] -> [committees])

# Constraints
Implies(serves(Guzman) == finance, serves(Hawking) == incentives) ::: If Guzman serves on the finance committee, then Hawking serves on the incentives committee
Implies(serves(Lepp) == finance, And(serves(Miyauchi) == incentives, serves(Upchurch) == incentives)) ::: If Lepp serves on the finance committee, then Miyauchi and Upchurch both serve on the incentives committee
Not(And(serves(Wharton) == finance, serves(Zhu) == finance)) ::: Wharton serves on a different committee from the one on which Zhu serves
Not(And(serves(Upchurch) == finance, serves(Guzman) == finance)) ::: Upchurch serves on a different committee from the one on which Guzman serves
Implies(serves(Zhu) == finance, serves(Hawking) == finance) ::: If Zhu serves on the finance committee, so does Hawking

# Options
Question ::: If Guzman serves on the incentives committee, then which one of the following must be true?
is_valid(serves(Lepp) == incentives) ::: (B)

context: Eight people—Fiona, George, Harriet, Ingrid, Karl, Manuel, Olivia, and Peter—are sitting, evenly spaced, around a circular picnic table. Any two of them are said to be sitting directly across from one another if and only if there are exactly three other people sitting between them, counting in either direction around the table. The following conditions apply: Fiona sits directly across from George. Harriet sits immediately next to neither Fiona nor Karl. Ingrid sits immediately next to, and immediately clockwise from, Olivia.
question: Which one of the following could be the order in which four of the people are seated, with no one else seated between them, counting clockwise around the table?
options: A) George, Peter, Karl, Fiona
B) Harriet, Olivia, Ingrid, Karl
C) Ingrid, Fiona, Peter, Manuel
D) Olivia, Manuel, Karl, George
E) Peter, Harriet, Karl, Fiona
raw_logic_programs:
# Declarations
people = EnumSort([Fiona, George, Harriet, Ingrid, Karl, Manuel, Olivia, Peter])
positions = EnumSort([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8])
seated = Function([people] -> [positions])

# Constraints
And(seated(Fiona) == (seated(George) + 4) % 8, seated(George) == (seated(Fiona) + 4) % 8) ::: Fiona sits directly across from George
ForAll([p:people], Not(Implies(seated(p) == (seated(Harriet) + 1) % 8, p == Fiona) And Not(Implies(seated(p) == (seated(Harriet) - 1) % 8, p == Fiona)))) ::: Harriet sits immediately next to neither Fiona nor Karl
And(seated(Ingrid) == (seated(Olivia) + 1) % 8, seated(Olivia) == (seated(Ingrid) - 1) % 8) ::: Ingrid sits immediately next to, and immediately clockwise from, Olivia

# Options
Question ::: Which one of the following could be the order in which four of the people are seated, with no one else seated between them, counting clockwise around the table?
is_exception(is_sat(And(seated(George) == 1, seated(Peter) == 2, seated(Karl) == 3, seated(Fiona) == 4))) ::: (A)
is_exception(is_sat(And(seated(Harriet) == 1, seated(Olivia) == 2, seated(Ingrid) == 3, seated(Karl) == 4))) ::: (B)
is_exception(is_sat(And(seated(Ingrid) == 1, seated(Fiona) == 2, seated(Peter) == 3, seated(Manuel) == 4))) ::: (C)
is_exception(is_sat(And(seated(Olivia) == 1, seated(Manuel) == 2, seated(Karl) == 3, seated(George) == 4))) ::: (D)
is_exception(is_sat(And(seated(Peter) == 1, seated(Harriet) == 2, seated(Karl) == 3, seated(Fiona) == 4))) ::: (E)

Ingrid sits immediately next to, and immediately clockwise from, Olivia.
question: If Harriet and Olivia each sits immediately next to George, then which one of the following could be the two people each of whom sits immediately next to Peter?
options: A) Fiona and Karl
B) Fiona and Olivia
C) Harriet and Ingrid
D) Harriet and Karl
E) Karl and Manuel
raw_logic_programs:
# Declarations
people = EnumSort([Fiona, George, Harriet, Ingrid, Karl, Manuel, Olivia, Peter])
position = IntSort()
seats = Function([people] -> [position])

# Constraints
Abs(seats(Fiona) - seats(George)) == 4 ::: Fiona sits directly across from George
And(Not(Abs(seats(Harriet) - seats(Fiona)) == 1), Not(Abs(seats(Harriet) - seats(Karl)) == 1)) ::: Harriet sits immediately next to neither Fiona nor Karl
Or(And(seats(Ingrid) == seats(Olivia) + 1, seats(Olivia) < 8), And(seats(Olivia) == 8, seats(Ingrid) == 1)) ::: Ingrid sits immediately next to, and immediately clockwise from, Olivia
And(Abs(seats(Harriet) - seats(George)) == 1, Abs(seats(Olivia) - seats(George)) == 1) ::: Harriet and Olivia each sit immediately next to George
ForAll([p:people], 1 <= seats(p) <= 8) ::: each person has a position between 1 and 8
Distinct([p:people], seats(p)) ::: each position is unique

# Options
Question ::: Which one of the following could be the two people each of whom sits immediately next to Peter?
is_sat(And(Abs(seats(Fiona) - seats(Peter)) == 1, Abs(seats(Karl) - seats(Peter)) == 1)) ::: (A)
is_sat(And(Abs(seats(Fiona) - seats(Peter)) == 1, Abs(seats(Olivia) - seats(Peter)) == 1)) ::: (B)
is_sat(And(Abs(seats(Harriet) - seats(Peter)) == 1, Abs(seats(Ingrid) - seats(Peter)) == 1)) ::: (C)
is_sat(And(Abs(seats(Harriet) - seats(Peter)) == 1, Abs(seats(Karl) - seats(Peter)) == 1)) ::: (D)
is_sat(And(Abs(seats(Karl) - seats(Peter)) == 1, Abs(seats(Manuel) - seats(Peter)) == 1)) ::: (E)

context: A florist is filling a customer's order for three bouquets—bouquet 1, bouquet 2, and bouquet 3. Each of the bouquets is to be composed of one or more of five kinds of flowers—lilies, peonies, roses, snapdragons, and tulips—subject to the following conditions: Bouquets 1 and 3 cannot have any kind of flower in common. Bouquets 2 and 3 must have exactly two kinds of flowers in common. Bouquet 3 must have snapdragons. If a bouquet has lilies, that bouquet must also have roses but cannot have snapdragons. If a bouquet has tulips, that bouquet must also have peonies.
question: If lilies are in bouquet 1, which one of the following must
options: A) Lilies are in bouquet 2.

C) Roses are in bouquet 2.
D) Tulips are in bouquet 2.
E) Tulips are in bouquet 3.

options: A) Flynn cannot be on desk duty on Thursday.
B) Only Flynn or Hill can be on desk duty on Monday.

And(on_duty(Flynn) < on_duty(Kitson), on_duty(Flynn) < on_duty(Moore)) ::: original constraint

is_sat(ForAll([l:librarians], Implies(l == Moore or l == Zahn, on_duty(Flynn) < on_duty(l)))) ::: (E)
